overview: This enum identifies the status effect carried by a BuffDebuffDataTable row and selects the rule that stores, times, queries, or removes that effect.

None.simple: No status effect kind is assigned.
None.technical: The BuffDebuff row constructor defaults BuffDebuff to None, and FGameCharacterBuffDebuffRecord defaults Type to None. No exported row uses None. ApplyBuffDebuffRow has no case for None, so such a row would skip the type switch and only run the notification tail.

CP_010_Passive.simple: A character passive that makes dashing cheaper and changes dash rigidity as cursed energy rises.
CP_010_Passive.technical: OnCursedEnergyLevelChanged applies BUFF_CP_010_PASSIVE_2 at level 2 and BUFF_CP_010_PASSIVE_3 at levels 3 and 4, and removes the type at level 1. Exported rows use FloatValue[0] of 0.9 or 0.8 for dash gauge consumption and FloatValue[1] of 1.1 or 1.2 for dash end, dash begin, air begin, and air end rigidity rates.

Coercion.simple: A limited-use state that changes the cursed energy aura and spends one use on a special attack.
Coercion.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow truncates FloatValue[0] into RemainingBuffApplications and stores one stack. A CP_020 attack checks the stack, plays FX_CP_020_00211, then decrements one application. UpdateCursedEnergyAura replaces the level aura with FX_CP_020_00341 while a stack exists. Removing Coercion refreshes the level aura and can refresh slot effects after defeat.

Hairpin_1.simple: The first Hairpin stage planted on an opponent.
Hairpin_1.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow stores one stack and caps the combined Hairpin stages at three, replacing a lower stage when full. GetBuffDebuffRecords reports FloatValue[0], which is 1.4 in the exported row. The CP_040 detonation selects CP_040_ATTACKG_02_01_1 and FX_CP_040_06511 for this stage. Hairpin states are removed when the applier is defeated.

Hairpin_2.simple: The second Hairpin stage planted on an opponent.
Hairpin_2.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow stores one stack and treats this stage as higher than Hairpin_1 when replacing a lower stage at the three-stage cap. GetBuffDebuffRecords reports FloatValue[0], which is 1.4 in the exported row. The CP_040 detonation selects CP_040_ATTACKG_02_01_2 and FX_CP_040_06521 for this stage.

Hairpin_3.simple: The third Hairpin stage planted on an opponent.
Hairpin_3.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow stores one stack and allows this stage to replace Hairpin_1 or Hairpin_2 at the three-stage cap. GetBuffDebuffRecords reports FloatValue[0], which is 1.4 in the exported row. The CP_040 detonation selects CP_040_ATTACKG_02_01_3 and FX_CP_040_06531 for this stage.

Resonance_1.simple: The first Resonance stage detected on an opponent.
Resonance_1.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow stores one stack and caps the combined Resonance stages at three. GetBuffDebuffRecords reports FloatValue[0], which is 1.5 in the exported row. CP_040 checks stages in descending order and selects CP_040_ATTACKH_02_01_1 and FX_CP_040_07411 when only this stage is present.

Resonance_2.simple: The second Resonance stage detected on an opponent.
Resonance_2.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow stores one stack and treats this stage as higher than Resonance_1 when a lower stage is replaced at the three-stage cap. GetBuffDebuffRecords reports FloatValue[0], which is 1.5 in the exported row. CP_040 selects CP_040_ATTACKH_02_01_2 and FX_CP_040_07421 when this is the highest stage present.

Resonance_3.simple: The third Resonance stage detected on an opponent.
Resonance_3.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow stores one stack and lets this stage replace either lower stage at the three-stage cap. GetBuffDebuffRecords reports FloatValue[0], which is 1.5 in the exported row. CP_040 tests this stage first and selects CP_040_ATTACKH_02_01_3 and FX_CP_040_07431.

CP_040_Passive.simple: A passive that stays active while Hairpin or Resonance marks remain on opponents.
CP_040_Passive.technical: OnBuffDebuffAppliedToTarget adds BUFF_CP_040_PASSIVE when the owner applies any Hairpin or Resonance type. ActionTick removes it once no opponent carries those marks from that owner. OnDamageDealt uses its buff record to play the passive icon action when the receiver is marked and the damage row grants attacker cursed energy experience.

CP_051_Passive.simple: A passive that upgrades Cursed Energy Attack 2 and briefly changes its speed and damage.
CP_051_Passive.technical: The passive is restored on revival and selects CP_051_ATTACKH_2_1 through CP_051_ATTACKH_2_3 for the attack set. The boosted attack uses owner unique float 9 slot 0 as its damage rate and unique float 7 slot 0 as its beam speed multiplier. Applying it spawns FX_CP_051_00311 in effect slot 2 and removing it clears that slot. GetCP230SpeedRate uses FloatValue[0], which is 1.2 in the exported row.

CP_060_Passive.simple: A gauge-level passive that improves jumping and falling control.
CP_060_Passive.technical: OnGauge27CLevelChanged applies BUFF_CP_060_PASSIVE_2 at gauge level 2 and BUFF_CP_060_PASSIVE_3 at levels 3 and 4. The rows set FloatValue[0] to 1.1 or 1.2 for movement speed, FloatValue[1] to 1.05 or 1.1 for fall gravity, FloatValue[2] to 1.05 or 1.1 for jump animation, FloatValue[3] to 1.25 or 1.34 for jump power, and FloatValue[4] to 2.0 or 2.5 for fall gravity while a jump action is active.

CP_081_Passive.simple: A guard-linked passive that increases jump power, movement, and falling speed.
CP_081_Passive.technical: ApplyPassiveBuff applies BUFF_CP_081_PASSIVE_1 through _3 by cursed energy level, and EndGuardEffect removes the type. The exported rows use FloatValue[0] of 1.3 for movement, FloatValue[1] of 1.2 for jump animation, FloatValue[2] of 1.5 for jump power, and FloatValue[3] of 2.75 for fall gravity while jumping.

CP_090_Passive.simple: A timed passive that improves cursed energy recovery and dash economy.
CP_090_Passive.technical: ApplyPassiveLevel applies the level 1, 2, or 3 row when the passive is absent, and ActionTick can start it inside the character unique time window. GetCursedEnergyExpRecoverWithTimeValue adds FloatValue[0] times the final level threshold every second, using 0.1 in every exported row. FloatValue[1] is 1.2 for dash speed, FloatValue[2] is 0.9, 0.85, or 0.8 for dash gauge consumption, and FloatValue[3] is 1.5, 1.8, or 2.0 for cursed energy recovery.

CP_100_Passive.simple: A timed passive gained after engaging two nearby targets, improving movement and dash cost.
CP_100_Passive.technical: The action controller applies BUFF_CP_100_PASSIVE_1 through _3 by cursed energy level when exactly two valid targets are found. The exported rows set FloatValue[0] to 10 seconds of duration, FloatValue[1] to 1.1, 1.15, or 1.2 for movement speed, and FloatValue[2] to 0.9, 0.85, or 0.8 for dash gauge consumption.

CP_110_CursedEnergyAttack2.simple: A toggle buff that powers the alternate Cursed Energy Attack 2 string.
CP_110_CursedEnergyAttack2.technical: SetCursedEnergyAttack2Active adds BUFF_CP_110_CURSEDENERGYATTACK2 on a homing start when no stack exists and removes the type when toggled off. While stacked, normal attacks use the CP_110_ATTACKD_2 attack set and attack row index 1. The exported row adds FloatValue[0] of 13 to outgoing guard durability damage and uses FloatValue[1] of 1.3 as a guard durability damage rate.

CP_110_Passive.simple: A passive that strengthens attacks and reduces incoming damage and guard damage.
CP_110_Passive.technical: SetPassiveActive adds BUFF_CP_110_PASSIVE and restores the saved cursed energy gauge on deactivation. Normal attack notifies use the stack to set action flags directly. The exported row uses FloatValue[1] of 1.2 for attack rate, FloatValue[2] of 0.95 for received damage, and FloatValue[3] of 0.9 for both guard durability damage received and guard durability damage sent.

DomainExpansion_CP_130.simple: The domain expansion user state for CP_130.
DomainExpansion_CP_130.technical: BeginSequenceTarget resolves BUFF_DOMAINEXPANSION_CP_130_USER and applies it to the caster, while RemoveDomainBuffDebuffs resolves the same row and removes its type. The exported row sets FloatValue[0] to 1.2, which multiplies cursed energy recovery and incoming guard durability damage. This state has no duration case in GetBuffDebuffDuration and stays until domain cleanup.

DomainExpansion_CP_130_Enemy.simple: The enemy state applied during the CP_130 domain expansion.
DomainExpansion_CP_130_Enemy.technical: BeginSequenceTarget resolves DEBUFF_DOMAINEXPANSION_CP_130_ENEMY and applies it to each rival with the caster as source. The exported row uses FloatValue[0] of 0.9 for movement speed and FloatValue[1] of 0.6 for cursed energy recovery. The state is replaced on reapplication and removed by domain cleanup.

DomainExpansion_CP_140.simple: The domain expansion user state for CP_140.
DomainExpansion_CP_140.technical: BeginSequenceTarget resolves BUFF_DOMAINEXPANSION_CP_140_USER and applies it to the caster. The exported row sets FloatValue[0] to 0.9 for cursed energy recovery, FloatValue[1] to 1.1 for movement, and FloatValue[2] to 0.6 for dash gauge consumption. Domain cleanup removes this type from the caster.

DomainExpansion_CP_140_Enemy.simple: The enemy state applied during the CP_140 domain expansion.
DomainExpansion_CP_140_Enemy.technical: BeginSequenceTarget resolves DEBUFF_DOMAINEXPANSION_CP_140_ENEMY and applies it to each rival. The exported row sets FloatValue[0] to 5 seconds for the recurring burn, FloatValue[1] to 0.9 for movement speed, and FloatValue[2] to 1.2 for dash gauge consumption. TickBuffDebuffs sends CP_140_DEBUFF_BURN each time that interval expires while the state has no normal duration.

CP_140_Passive.simple: A low-health passive that raises cursed energy recovery and cursed technique damage.
CP_140_Passive.technical: CP_140 adds the row matching the current cursed energy level at low hit points and removes the type when the low-health condition ends. Exported rows use FloatValue[0] of 1.5, 1.8, or 2.0 for cursed energy recovery and FloatValue[1] of 1.1, 1.15, or 1.2 for attack rate on CursedEnergyAttack_1 and CursedEnergyAttack_2.

CP_150_Passive.simple: A passive that changes projectile behavior and lowers overall attack rate.
CP_150_Passive.technical: CP_150 applies BUFF_CP_150_PASSIVE during its special attack events. While stacked, projectile setup divides one unique float by level-specific owner values, and GetPassiveAttackRate multiplies attack rate by FloatValue[0], which is 0.5 in the exported row.

RotTechnique.simple: The setup debuff that lets CP_160 convert marked opponents into Decay stages.
RotTechnique.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow refuses a duplicate and adds a timed state with duration FloatValue[0] of -1 seconds from every exported row, so it persists by custom rules. If any Decay state exists on the target, applying RotTechnique adds FloatValue[1] to the decay gauge instead of adding another state. CP_160 reads the stack to select decaying opponents and later converts it into DEBUFF_DECAY_1, _2, or _3 according to cursed energy level. TickBuffDebuffs removes the state when its source is defeated.

Decay_1.simple: The first Decay stage created from RotTechnique.
Decay_1.technical: CP_160 converts RotTechnique to DEBUFF_DECAY_1 at cursed energy level 1 and removes RotTechnique. All three Decay rows export identical FloatValue data, with minus one at slot 0 and gauge-derived rates and intervals in slots 1 through 11. Decay_1 selects the CP_160_ATTACKH_02_01_1_n detonation set, feeds dash speed and gauge recovery rate tables, and emits CP_160_DEBUFF_DECAY when the gauge-derived interval is nonnegative. Removing any Decay type resets the gauge to zero and its cap to 150.

Decay_2.simple: The second Decay stage created from RotTechnique.
Decay_2.technical: CP_160 converts RotTechnique to DEBUFF_DECAY_2 at cursed energy level 2. This stage selects the CP_160_ATTACKH_02_01_2_n detonation set and shares the exported gauge-derived rate and interval layout with the other Decay stages. It uses the same negative slot 0 sentinel to suppress a periodic damage tick and the same gauge reset on removal.

Decay_3.simple: The third Decay stage created from RotTechnique.
Decay_3.technical: CP_160 converts RotTechnique to DEBUFF_DECAY_3 at cursed energy level 3. This stage selects the CP_160_ATTACKH_02_01_3_n detonation set. Its exported values match the other Decay stages, and it uses the same gauge-indexed dash speed, gauge recovery, and damage tick consumers.

CP_160_Passive.simple: A passive that marks the owner as having CP_160 shikigami support active.
CP_160_Passive.technical: CP_160 applies BUFF_CP_160_PASSIVE when it summons the shikigami and removes the type through the controller cleanup path. Status_IsBuffType and Status_IsDebuffType classify it as a buff, which controls whether its enabled row spawns or clears the buff aura.

MoveSlow.simple: A movement slow applied by attacks and other non-item sources.
MoveSlow.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow increments an existing stack up to four and replaces the state with the newly resolved row. GetBuffDebuffDuration reads FloatValue[Stack * 2 - 2] seconds, and GetMoveSpeedRate reads FloatValue[Stack * 2 - 1] as a multiplier. The general exported row uses 10, 11, 12, and 13 seconds with multipliers 0.9, 0.8, 0.75, and 0.7.

MoveSlowItem.simple: A movement slow applied by equipment effects.
MoveSlowItem.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses the same stack cap of four, even-slot seconds, and odd-slot rate multiplier as MoveSlow. The six exported item rows last 10 seconds at every stack and use multipliers 0.95, 0.9, 0.85, 0.8, 0.75, and 0.7. Item description text keeps the equipment effect value for this type because the formatter special-cases numeric type 0x1D.

HitPointRecoverWithTimeItem.simple: A timed item effect that gradually heals the owner.
HitPointRecoverWithTimeItem.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow replaces an existing state and uses FloatValue[0] as seconds. GetHitPointWithTimeValue sums FloatValue[1] from these states, and Tick applies that value multiplied by DeltaTime each frame. The six exported rows use durations 20, 20, 30, 30, 40, and 40 seconds with per-second values 0.1, 0.2, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5.

CursedEnergyRecoverSlow.simple: A stacking debuff that slows cursed energy recovery.
CursedEnergyRecoverSlow.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow increments an existing stack up to four. GetBuffDebuffDuration reads FloatValue[Stack * 2 - 2] seconds, and GetCursedEnergyRecoverRate reads FloatValue[Stack * 2 - 1] as the recovery multiplier. The exported row uses 10, 11, 12, and 13 seconds with multipliers 0.9, 0.7, 0.65, and 0.5.

CursedEnergyExpIncrease.simple: A revival buff that raises cursed energy experience gain.
CursedEnergyExpIncrease.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow replaces an existing state, uses FloatValue[0] as 30 seconds, and marks nonpositive durations with bNoDuration. GetCursedEnergyExpRate multiplies experience gain by FloatValue[1], which is 1.2 in the exported row. Status_IsBuffType classifies it as a buff for aura handling.

CursedEnergyExpIncreaseItem.simple: A timed item effect that raises cursed energy experience gain.
CursedEnergyExpIncreaseItem.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow replaces an existing state and uses FloatValue[0] as seconds. GetCursedEnergyExpRate reads FloatValue[1] as a multiplier. The six exported rows use 10, 10, 10, 15, 15, and 15 seconds with multipliers 1.05, 1.1, 1.15, 1.2, 1.25, and 1.3.

CursedEnergyExpDecreaseItem.simple: A timed item effect intended to reduce cursed energy experience gain.
CursedEnergyExpDecreaseItem.technical: GetCursedEnergyExpRate reads FloatValue[1] from this state as a rate multiplier, and ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as seconds. The exported rows set durations of 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40 seconds but leave FloatValue[1] at zero, so the sampled data does not encode the intended reduced rate.

DashDisabledItem.simple: A timed item effect that prevents dashing.
DashDisabledItem.technical: CanDash inlines a stack query for this type and returns false whenever the total is greater than zero, even with dash gauge remaining. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration, and the six exported rows last 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and 13 seconds.

DashGaugeUnlimitedItem.simple: A timed item effect that removes dash gauge consumption.
DashGaugeUnlimitedItem.technical: GetDashGaugeConsumeRateFromEffects inlines a stack query for this type and forces the final consumption rate to zero when the total is greater than zero. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration, and the six exported rows last 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40 seconds.

DashGaugeRecoverIncreaseItem.simple: A timed item effect that speeds up dash gauge recovery.
DashGaugeRecoverIncreaseItem.technical: GetDashGaugeRecoverRate multiplies the recovery rate by FloatValue[1]. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration. The exported rows last 30, 45, 60, 65, 70, and 75 seconds with multipliers 1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, and 1.5.

DashGaugeRecoverDecreaseItem.simple: A timed item effect that slows dash gauge recovery.
DashGaugeRecoverDecreaseItem.technical: GetDashGaugeRecoverRate multiplies the recovery rate by FloatValue[1] and clamps the final rate at zero. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration. All six exported rows last 20 seconds with multipliers 0.95, 0.9, 0.85, 0.8, 0.75, and 0.7.

DashGaugeNotRecoverItem.simple: A timed item effect that pauses dash gauge recovery.
DashGaugeNotRecoverItem.technical: Tick checks GetBuffDebuffStack for this type and skips the entire dash gauge recovery block while at least one stack exists. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration, and the three exported rows last 5, 10, and 15 seconds.

SendDamageIncreaseItem.simple: A timed item effect that increases damage dealt.
SendDamageIncreaseItem.technical: GetSendAttackDamageRate multiplies outgoing damage by FloatValue[1]. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration. All six exported rows last 45 seconds with multipliers 1.05, 1.1, 1.15, 1.2, 1.25, and 1.3.

SendDamageDecreaseItem.simple: A timed item effect that reduces damage dealt.
SendDamageDecreaseItem.technical: GetSendAttackDamageRate multiplies outgoing damage by FloatValue[1]. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration. The exported rows last 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40 seconds with multipliers 0.8, 0.75, 0.7, 0.65, 0.6, and 0.55.

ReceiveDamageDecreaseItem.simple: A timed item effect that reduces damage taken.
ReceiveDamageDecreaseItem.technical: GetReceiveDamageRate multiplies incoming damage by FloatValue[1] for damage rows whose attack type is not Debuff. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration. All six exported rows last 45 seconds with multipliers 0.95, 0.9, 0.85, 0.8, 0.75, and 0.7.

ReceiveDamageWithTimeItem.simple: A timed item effect that continuously drains health.
ReceiveDamageWithTimeItem.technical: GetHitPointWithTimeValue sums FloatValue[1] from these states together with healing item values, and Tick applies that sum multiplied by DeltaTime every frame. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration. All six exported rows last 15 seconds with per-second values of minus 0.1, 0.2, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5.

LinkComboCursedEnergyExpIncreaseItem.simple: A timed item effect that increases cursed energy gained from link combos.
LinkComboCursedEnergyExpIncreaseItem.technical: AddLinkComboCursedEnergy adds FloatValue[1] to a starting multiplier of one before applying the character link combo rate. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration. The six exported rows last 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 seconds and all use a multiplier of 2.0.

SuperArmorItem.simple: A timed item effect that grants super armor.
SuperArmorItem.technical: IsSuperArmorActive scans all states and returns true when any state has this type, regardless of the separate bSuperArmorActive flag. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration, and the six exported rows last 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 seconds.

CursedEnergyRecoverIncrease.simple: A timed buff that increases cursed energy recovery.
CursedEnergyRecoverIncrease.technical: GetCursedEnergyRecoverRate adds FloatValue[1] to the recovery rate and subtracts one. ApplyBuffDebuffRow uses FloatValue[0] as duration, and the exported row lasts 30 seconds with a multiplier of 2.0. A character AI tick also reads the stack count.

CP_170_Passive.simple: A passive that strengthens attacks against a character who targets the owner.
CP_170_Passive.technical: ActionTick adds BUFF_CP_170_PASSIVE while the owner can act and the current or secondary target targets the owner, and removes it otherwise. GetCP170PassiveRate uses FloatValue[0] of 1.1 and GetCP170PassiveRate1 uses FloatValue[1] of 1.2 in the exported row. The first rate is passed into collision parameters for attacks.

CP_180_Passive.simple: A timed passive that improves movement and selects a stronger attack set.
CP_180_Passive.technical: Applying this type spawns FX_CP_180_00101 and FX_CP_180_00102 at the waist, with the second held in effect slot 2. Removal clears that slot and plays FX_CP_180_00103. Normal attacks use a CP_180-specific attack set while the stack exists. Exported rows last 10 seconds and use FloatValue[1] of 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 for movement speed.

CP_200_Passive.simple: A timed passive that makes dashing cheaper.
CP_200_Passive.technical: CP_200 applies BUFF_CP_200_PASSIVE after its cursed energy or experience event. The exported row lasts 35 seconds and sets FloatValue[1] to 0.6 for dash gauge consumption. The type is classified as a buff for aura handling and replaces an existing state of the same type.

CP_190_Passive.simple: A passive that reduces the cost of a blood manipulation resource.
CP_190_Passive.technical: SpendUnknown2C8 reads the stack and selects owner unique float 2 slot 0 as the spend rate, with 1.0 used when the passive is absent. The exported row has no nonzero FloatValue entries, so all cost scaling for this passive comes from owner unique data.

CP_210_Passive.simple: A passive that marks the owner as having the weapon drawn.
CP_210_Passive.technical: SetWeaponDrawn adds BUFF_CP_210_PASSIVE when the weapon is drawn and removes the type when it is sheathed. The exported row has no nonzero FloatValue entries, and the type is classified as a buff for aura handling.

CP_220_Passive_Weak.simple: The weaker form of the CP_220 stance passive.
CP_220_Passive_Weak.technical: CP_220 selects owner unique variant 1 when only this stack is present, and variant 2 when the Strong stack is also present. The exported row lasts 15 seconds, uses FloatValue[1] of 0.4 for cursed energy recovery, and FloatValue[2] of 0.85 for movement. Applying either stance refreshes the passive aura.

CP_220_Passive_Strong.simple: The stronger form of the CP_220 stance passive.
CP_220_Passive_Strong.technical: CP_220 selects owner unique variant 2 while this stack is present. ApplyBuffDebuffRow removes a Weak state first and refreshes an existing Strong state to full duration instead of stacking both. The exported row lasts 15 seconds, uses FloatValue[1] of 0.25 for cursed energy recovery, and FloatValue[2] of 0.7 for movement.

CP_230_CursedEnergyAttack1.simple: A toggle buff that powers the alternate Cursed Energy Attack 1 string.
CP_230_CursedEnergyAttack1.technical: StartAttackHoming toggles BUFF_CP_230_CURSEDENERGYATTACK1 on when no stack exists and off otherwise. While stacked, normal attacks use a boosted set and the status controller reports FloatValue[0] of 1.2 as an extra speed rate, FloatValue[1] of 1.15 as an attack rate through a function named GetCP240PassiveRate, FloatValue[2] of 1.15 as dash speed, and FloatValue[3] of 0.5 as dash gauge consumption.

CP_240_Passive.simple: A passive that improves dash speed, cursed energy recovery, and rigidity.
CP_240_Passive.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow stores one stack and copies FloatValue[5] into IconCapacity. Exported rows use FloatValue[0] of 1.1, 1.2, or 1.35 for dash speed, FloatValue[1] of 0.9, 0.8, or 0.6 for dash gauge consumption, FloatValue[2] and FloatValue[3] of 1.1 and 0.9 or stronger pairs for dash rigidity, FloatValue[4] of 1.2, 1.4, or 1.6 for cursed energy recovery, and IconCapacity values 1, 2, or 3.

CP_250_Passive.simple: A passive that scales attack and cursed energy experience output.
CP_250_Passive.technical: GetBuffDebuffAttackRate reads FloatValue[0] and GetCursedEnergyExpRate reads FloatValue[1]. All three exported rows currently set both slots to 1.0, so the sampled data encodes neutral multipliers. The type is classified as a buff and replaces an existing state of the same type.

CP_260_Passive.simple: A passive that activates when two or more opponents target the owner.
CP_260_Passive.technical: ActionTick adds BUFF_CP_260_PASSIVE while the owner is alive, input is enabled, and at least two opponents target the owner. While stacked, GetReceiveDamageRate uses FloatValue[0] of 0.7 for attacks other than SuperCursedEnergyAttack and SpecialTagCombo, and GetGuardDurabilityDamageRate returns zero.

CN_230_Passive.simple: A limited-use passive that enables a revival and a special hit set.
CN_230_Passive.technical: SetupPassives adds BUFF_CN_230_PASSIVE or BUFF_CN_230_PASSIVE_ST according to unique mode. ApplyBuffDebuffRow truncates FloatValue[0] into RemainingBuffApplications, giving six or three uses, and TryAnswerDamage consumes one use on revival. While stacked, specific hit names count as passive effect hits for non-super attacks.

CN_250_Passive.simple: A one-use low-health passive that enables a healing extra attack.
CN_250_Passive.technical: OnHitPointChanged applies BUFF_CN_250_PASSIVE once the hit point ratio reaches the character unique threshold. FCN_250_ExtraAttack_1 converts that state into a hit point heal based on level-specific owner unique values, then removes the type and marks the passive consumed.

IceFormation_Begin.simple: The setup state that starts ice gauge decay on opponents.
IceFormation_Begin.technical: SetupPassives resolves DEBUFF_ICE_FORMATION_BEGIN and applies it to every opponent with CN_250 as source. ApplyBuffDebuffRow does not store a state for this type, instead assigning FloatValue[0] of 10 to IceFormationGaugeDecayRate and FloatValue[1] of 2 seconds to IceFormationDecayDelay. TickBuffDebuffs subtracts DeltaTime times the decay rate from the ice gauge after the delay expires.

IceFormation_Damage.simple: The state that adds ice gauge and raises the ice formation level.
IceFormation_Damage.technical: Damage rows CN_250_ATTACKA_01_01 through CN_250_ATTACKF_01_01 resolve exported DEBUFF_ICE_FORMATION_ATTACK rows and apply them through the standard hit path. ApplyBuffDebuffRow adds FloatValue[0] to IceFormationGaugeValue, capped at 300, and converts gauge times 0.01 into a level. When the level rises it applies DEBUFF_ICE_FORMATION and resets the decay delay. Exported attack amounts are 2, 10, 10, 15, 30, 70, and 100.

IceFormation_Debuff.simple: The active ice formation state that slows movement and jumping.
IceFormation_Debuff.technical: ApplyBuffDebuffRow stores one state and refuses a duplicate. GetMoveSpeedRate uses FloatValue[IceFormationLevel - 1], and GetJumpPowerRate uses FloatValue[IceFormationLevel + 2], with exported values 0.95, 0.85, and 0.6 for movement and 0.95, 0.85, and 0.65 for jumping. TickBuffDebuffs removes the state when the gauge reaches zero or the source is defeated and lowers the level as the gauge decays. Removal resets the gauge to zero, the level to zero, and the cap to 300.

Adapt_CursedEnergyAttack_1.simple: An adaptation that nullifies Cursed Energy Attack 1 damage.
Adapt_CursedEnergyAttack_1.technical: When the receiver carries this stack and the damage row has DamageAdaptType CursedEnergyAttack_1, CN_240 returns zero damage. CP_020 requires both this adaptation and CursedEnergyAttack_2 to enable the variation cursed technique. The state is kept by the domain expansion caster cleanup list and shown in the battle adaptation icon UI.

Adapt_CursedEnergyAttack_2.simple: An adaptation that nullifies Cursed Energy Attack 2 damage.
Adapt_CursedEnergyAttack_2.technical: When the receiver carries this stack and the damage row has DamageAdaptType CursedEnergyAttack_2, CN_240 returns zero damage. CP_160 uses the stack to make listed CP_160 decay damage rows unadaptable on decayed targets. CN_240 also knocks the owner away when a Decay state comes from a source with this adaptation.

Adapt_ExtraAttack.simple: An adaptation that nullifies Extra Attack damage.
Adapt_ExtraAttack.technical: When the receiver carries this stack and the damage row has DamageAdaptType ExtraAttack, CN_240 returns zero damage. CP_020 requires the adaptation for its variation cursed technique, and the battle notify widget detects when this type first appears. The state is displayed by the battle adaptation icon UI.

Adapt_TagCombo.simple: An adaptation that enables assisted hit decisions when teammates are present.
Adapt_TagCombo.technical: The traced normal attack and character-specific hit gates return true when another eligible same-team character exists and this stack is present. Several action controllers read the stack to allow or force those tag combo attack decisions. The state is preserved for the domain caster cleanup list.

Invalid.technical: Invalid is declared as the numeric sentinel 255 in the enum header. No source consumer references the Invalid member, and no exported BuffDebuffDataTable row uses it, so its runtime handling cannot be established from the available static evidence.

notes: The enum is uint8. The listed members occupy contiguous values from 0 through 67, and Invalid is 255. No exported BuffDebuffDataTable row uses None or Invalid.
ApplyBuffDebuffRow copies the resolved row into a state and uses the enum to choose replacement, stacking, duration, gauge, and side-effect behavior.
Status_IsBuffType and Status_IsDebuffType classify most members, with unlisted values treated as debuffs for enabled aura checks.
FloatValue indices are type-specific. Traced consumers use some slots for seconds and others for rate multipliers, so slot meanings cannot be shared across enum members.
